name: Pictology
hero_text: Hand-written pysanky, heirloom ornaments, felt and fiber pieces, and one-of-a-kind cards, made by Carole using the old wax-and-dye method, one line at a time.
about_teaser: I'm a folk artist in Brattleboro, Vermont, and a grandma who never quite stopped playing with color. Mostly I write pysanky (Ukrainian wax-and-dye eggs), but you'll also find ornaments, felt flowers and handmade cards coming off my kitchen table.
about_body: I make art under the name Pictology from my home in Brattleboro, Vermont. My first love is pysanky, the Ukrainian tradition of writing on eggs with beeswax and dye. No paint: each line is drawn in hot wax, the egg goes into a dye bath, and the design builds up color by color until the wax is melted away to reveal it. I studied American Studies and Folklore at Marlboro College, and those old symbols still fascinate me: suns for life, deer for prosperity, waves for good fortune, roosters for a new day. Lately I also letter little verses and landscapes onto my eggs, stitch felt flowers, and make cards just for fun. Every piece is one of a kind.
contact_blurb: Ornaments, gift eggs, custom lettering for a wedding or new baby, or a set of cards: send Carole a note about what you have in mind.
meta_description: Pictology: hand-dyed pysanky eggs, ornaments, fiber art and handmade cards by Carole, Brattleboro, Vermont.
